sections.overview: The tube-eye is a rare, deep-water fish and the sole living member of its family.
sections.identification: It has tubular eyes, protrusible jaws and extremely elongated lower tail rays.
sections.habitat: It is meso- to bathypelagic, recorded at roughly 300–800 metres in tropical and temperate seas.
sections.diet: It feeds on small crustaceans, including copepods.
sections.behavior: It may swim head-up while feeding; some observations suggest daily changes in depth.
sections.ecology: Spanish-language fish lists call it ojibrotado; English references use tube-eye.
sections.conservation: The consulted FAO account reports no fishery for this elusive species.
